- Analyse previous year question papers carefully — certain areas consistently carry high difficulty levels. Focus more on those areas while preparing. Remember, it’s not during practice but in the exam when those 35 questions from QA and LRDI feel overwhelming due to the pressure and time crunch. That’s when your preparation truly gets tested. So, go beyond standard practice — solve slightly tougher questions, even from JEE Main level, to build that extra edge.
- Also, for interviews, make sure to prepare from the pgdba.ml website — it has a good collection of previous year interview questions. Go through them thoroughly to get a clear idea of what kind of questions are usually asked. This will help you stay one step ahead and reduce the surprise factor during the actual interview.
- Confidence is built not just by accuracy, but by being comfortable under pressure and knowing the terrain well — both in the exam and in the interview And make sure that u put u r effort at the right areas

records.tips:
- Please revise math thoroughly, use JEE Mains math textbooks for calculus/Algebra/Probability/Coordinate geometry (like cengage for example)
- it will quite literally carry the written score
- Please aim to score a bit higher in the written test if the Acads are on the lower end / Work experience is less than 1.5 years.
- For the interview. Please don't panic and try to remember/learn/cram everything in the weeks following up to the interview. If you're a fresher, be very thorough with your math skills.
- Interview for the higher work ex folks 1.5+

- Be very clear of your goals ( what you expect from the course et al) and how it's going to help you in the long run. Your job is to convince them that your aim and intent is clear.
- (I have noticed that aspirants fumble hard during the interview because they are not clear as to why they're doing this, money, is obviously a thing, but that cannot be the only driving factor)
- (I had made it very clear to the panel that I don't want to be siloed as a purely operations resource and explained how this course would help me be more resourceful and help a diverse set of domains. This was in relations to my work ex)
